title: P2P-fallback and link-selection tail-latency investigation
body:
Purpose:
Quick investigation notes and hypotheses for tail-latency spikes that correlate with GPU peer-to-peer (P2P) fallback and link-selection decisions in mixed NVLink/PCIe topologies. Goal: identify reproducible test matrix, root causes, and mitigation ideas we can take into production scheduling/placement heuristics for Dedicated and Private clusters.

Background/context:
- Several customer incidents and internal benchmarks showed 95th/99th token latency regressions despite steady median. Suspect cross-domain transfers that cannot use NVLink (or GPUDirect) are falling back to host-staging, introducing host CPU / PCIe contention and interrupt bursts.
- Single-node NVLink-connected replicas show stable tails; adding a rack-adjacent GPU across a PCIe domain increases tail stdev.

Hypothesis summary (ranked):
1) Link-selection fallback from NVLink/P2P to host-staging for certain tensor transfer patterns causes microbursts on the PCIe root complex leading to queueing and interrupts that amplify tail latency.
2) NCCL (and other collective stacks) heuristics sometimes choose suboptimal interconnects in heterogeneous topologies (mixed NVLink islands + PCIe hops) when multiple rings/endpoints exist, causing unexpected serialization.
3) NUMA/CPU affinity and RX/TX channel saturation on the host side (small memcpy bursts) amplify tail latencies for small-packet frequent transfers (e.g., KV-cache lookups or small attention heads).

What we measured so far (summary):
- Workload: 6-sample batch of short-chat tokens (seq len 64) against a sharded GPT-like model using tensor-parallel sharding where certain layers require cross-GPU transfers of small tensors (~8-64KB) at high frequency.
- Topology: 4x A100 on node; GPUs 0-2 NVLinked, GPU 3 only PCIe-connected (simulating an island). Also cross-node case: 2x GPUs per node with RDMA disabled.
- Tools: nvml (nvidia-smi topo --matrix), nvprof/NSight (nvtx markers), perf + trace-cmd on host, tcpdump-like capture of PCIe events via ftrace tracepoints, and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO.
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, host memcpy bandwidth, PCIe bus utilization (relative), CPU irq counts during run.

Empirical observations (detailed):
- Single-node NVLink-only (0-2): median 8ms/token, p95 12ms, p99 18ms.
- Add island GPU (gpu3 via PCIe): median unchanged (~9ms), p95 jumps to 25ms, p99 to 62ms.
- Trace correlation shows sequences where small all-to-all transfers involving gpu3 are serviced via host staging: host memcpy bursts coincide with 99th percentile spikes.
- perf shows high irqctx_switch and elevated CPU busy on code paths handling DMA mapping and PCIe doorbell handling when fallback happens.
- NCCL logs show ring fallback and extra collectives created at runtime for compatibility; time spent waiting on host completion is nontrivial for small transfers.
- Enabling GPUDirect RDMA on same cross-node test reduced p99 by ~35% (but only when supported by network driver/hardware).

Root-cause candidates and evidence: 
- Missing or disabled GPUDirect paths (driver/firmware constraints) forces host bridging. Evidence: enabling GPUDirect or using NVLink island eliminates host memcpy phase and reduces spikes.
- NCCL ring selection chooses topologies that minimize aggregate bytes but ignore burst frequency — results in transfers batched into fewer host-staging operations which amplify instantaneous load. Evidence: logs show NCCL creating rings that include the PCIe-only GPU as the ring pivot.
- PCIe root-complex saturation and CPU-handled short-copy overhead dominate when transfer sizes are small and extremely frequent — host DMA setup/teardown overheads are high. Evidence: host tracing shows memcpy call rates and DMA mapping ops rising during p99 windows.

Quick experiments to validate (planned / in-progress):
1) Force disable P2P (cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess) vs forced enable and measure tail — isolate driver-level P2P degeneracy.
2) Run same workload but aggregate small transfers in the runtime to larger coalesced transfers (artificial micro-batching) and measure tail effect.
3) NCCL topology override (NCCL_ALGO=Ring/Tree, NCCL_TOPO) to force NVLink-first rings and compare.
4) Test with different PCIe gen (emulated by throttling) to see linearity of tail spikes.
5) Measure with IRQ affinity pinned away from host-side inference threads to check interrupt interference.

Commands/snippets we used: 
- nvidia-smi topo --matrix
- export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL; ./bench_infer --model sharded --batch 6 --seq 64 --nvtx
- sudo trace-cmd record -e dma_mapping -e dma_unmap -e irq_handler 
- perf stat -e cpu-clock,context-switches,irq_vectors -p <runtime_pid>

Mitigations / short-term fixes to test in staging: 
- Topology-aware placement: prefer grouping tensor shards to remain inside NVLink islands for latency-sensitive routes.
- Soft-rail scheduling: prefer to schedule latency-critical requests to replicas that avoid PCIe-hop GPUs; use routing policy to detect islands and fallback to other region.
- Conservative NCCL topology hints exposed to runtime: for mixed topologies, bias to NVLink-first rings even if slightly higher total traffic to reduce small-host-copy bursts.
- Coalescing micro-transfers in the runtime: implement a small-window aggregator for tiny tensors before sending across PCIe. Evaluate latency tradeoff.
- Improve host-side path: enable GPUDirect/RDMA where possible and ensure kernel/driver versions across fleet support it; tune IOMMU settings.

Operational notes and risks: 
- Changing placement heuristics will affect throughput/cost tradeoffs; need to expose as a policy knob (latency-priority vs throughput-priority).
- Coalescing adds extra latency for first tokens; must be adaptive and request-class aware.
- Enabling RDMA is constrained by hardware and network drivers; rollout will be phased.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What is the minimum coalescing window size that reduces p99 without adding >5% median latency? (micro experiments required)
- Can we detect P2P fallback at request time cheaply (NVML queries) to dynamically route requests away? How expensive is that check at scale?
- Are there specific NCCL versions/patches known to do better ring-selection with hetero-topologies? (ask infra/research)
- Should we add a runtime telemetry signal for "host-staging events" to collect at scale for Dedicated customers?

Next steps (owners):
- Marco: run NCCL topology override matrix and report p50/p95/p99 changes (due 2024-09-06).
- Jordan: micro-batching patch in runtime to coalesce small outgoing tensors (prototype by 2024-09-09).
- Priya: compile driver/firmware compatibility matrix for GPUDirect across our fleet images and note blockers (2024-09-05).
- Aisha (owner): consolidate results and propose placement policy change for latency-priority customers (draft by 2024-09-12).

Notes-to-self / miscellaneous observations: 
- When reproducing locally, NVSwitch machines behave very differently from DGX-style NVLink meshes — don't conflate the two.
- Watch out for perf noise; run each workload 10x and use trimmed-mean for comparison.
- Add NVTX ranges liberally in runtime to correlate logical phases with host trace windows.

Attachments/where to look: GH PR for prototype coalescing (linked), JIRA RT-7312 that tracks the customer incident, and the fleet matrix on Confluence that lists NIC/driver combos.

Status: draft note — planning experiments. Intentionally high-level but includes enough detail to reproduce locally.

Unresolved thought: maybe the runtime should build a small topology fingerprint (NVLink islands, pci-e hop counts) at startup and advertise it to the placement service so that low-latency routes are selected automatically.

END OF NOTE
